title: Maximising Every Student's Potential in Classrooms of the Future
what_it_is: Maximising Every Student's Potential in Classrooms of the Future

sections.label: Singapore form class sizes
sections.summary: Average and median form class sizes in Primary and Secondary schools range from 32 to 36.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Average and median form class sizes in Primary and Secondary schools range from 32 to 36.

sections.label: OECD class size fall
sections.summary: The overall class size in the OECD fell by 6.8% between 2000 and 2010 to a little over 20.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The overall class size in the OECD fell by 6.8% between 2000 and 2010 to a little over 20.

sections.label: British class size study
sections.summary: A 2008 British study of 22 primary and 27 secondary schools found low attaining students more than twice as likely to be disengaged in classes of 30 than 15.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A 2008 British study by Blatchford, Bassett and Brown with the University of London involving close observation of classrooms in 22 primary schools and 27 secondary schools concluded that low attaining students were more than twice as likely to be disengaged in classes of 30 students than they were in classes of 15.

sections.label: Proposed Singapore randomised trial
sections.summary: It suggests a large randomised trial in Singapore, similar to the Tennessee STAR project, to study reducing form class sizes to 20-25.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the issue is that academic evidence is divided, we suggest there should be a large randomised trial in Singapore, along similar lines to the massive, seminal Tennessee STAR project that is still being referred to by educators today, to study the impact of reducing average and median form class sizes to the 20-25 range.

sections.label: Urging smaller class trial
sections.summary: It urges a large randomised trial for smaller classes, targeting form class sizes of 20-25 as a mid-term goal using falling enrolments and stable teacher numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In summary, I urge the Government to conduct a large, randomised trial for smaller classes to determine the effects on academic achievement, levelling up poorer students in non-cognitive skills and attributes, such as confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the results are positive, we should target a form class size of 20-25 as a mid-term goal and use falling enrolments while keeping the number of teachers stable to make the changes necessary, so as to minimise cost increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The reduction in form class size should have a cascading effect to reduce the size of most classes as they currently exist, be they remedial or banded.

sections.label: MOE past class size cuts
sections.summary: MOE reduced average class sizes for Primary 1 in 2005 and Primary 2 in 2006, and in 2007 Parliament described the outcome as positive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MOE has reduced average class sizes before: for Primary 1 in 2005 and Primary 2 in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Parliament in 2007, the outcome of this class size reduction change was described by the Government as positive.

sections.label: Coding and technology enrichment
sections.summary: IMDA worked with schools to expose students to coding and technology, with "Code for Fun" benefiting 73,000 students since 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In the area of coding and technology, we worked with IMDA to expose students to basic coding and technology through various activities. "Code for Fun", for example, is an enrichment programme that has benefited 73,000 students in both Primary and Secondary schools since 2014.

sections.label: Applied Learning Programme in schools
sections.summary: The Applied Learning Programme is offered in all Secondary schools from this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Applied Learning Programme (ALP) is offered in all Secondary schools from this year.

sections.label: Differentiated subject levels
sections.summary: This year, Secondary school students can offer subjects at differentiated levels based on their strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: A major change we are making this year is to allow Secondary school students to offer subjects at differentiated levels, based on their strengths.

sections.label: Student Learning Space portal
sections.summary: From next year, all students will access quality learning resources through the new online Student Learning Space portal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: From next year, all students will be able to access quality learning resources through our Student Learning Space, which is a new online portal.

sections.label: Class sizes and pupil-teacher ratios
sections.summary: Teaching force grew 20% over the last decade, with pupil-teacher ratios of 16 and 12 for Primary and Secondary levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For example, John Hattie's work on the effects of class sizes says that these early advantages are not necessarily sustained.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: But what I can say is having grown our teaching force by 20% over the last decade, our current pupil-teacher ratios at 16 and 12 for Primary and Secondary school levels respectively are already comparable to OECD standards.

sections.label: Singapore Teaching Practice launched
sections.summary: This year, the Singapore Teaching Practice, a research-backed model of teaching and learning, was launched and will be adopted by NIE and schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For our teachers, we also invest in their continual professional development, because they are key.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This year, we launched the Singapore Teaching Practice (STP), our very own model of teaching and learning that is backed by research evidence and this will be adopted by NIE and in our schools.

sections.label: Values and character education
sections.summary: MOE is making changes guided by values and character education at the core of children's education, and Parliament adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: MOE is embarking on many exciting changes, but in all the things that we are doing, we are guided by values and character education that will always remain at the core of our children's education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With sound values, the right learning dispositions and the deep knowledge and skills, I am confident that our students can rise up to the opportunities and challenges of the future economy and Singaporean society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Resolved, "That Parliament do now adjourn." Adjourned accordingly at 7.28 pm.
